summary:
Podcast show notes for Episode 405 of Eptura's Workplace Innovator, hosted by Mike Petrusky, featuring David George, CEO and Founder of CRUX Workplace. George's background spans workplace design, facilities management, real estate management and strategy, and his firm co-creates flexible, high performing workplace designs intended to let people do their best work.

Core argument: workplace strategists should be involved from the outset of a project, before architects and designers, so that business processes are understood and translated into an effective design brief. George frames innovation as enabling people to perform at their best while also feeling joy and connection at work, rather than as a purely spatial or technology exercise.

On change management, George says engaging employees early in the design process produces higher acceptance and greater ownership of the resulting change. He identifies three pillars of successful change management: employee engagement, clear communication, and sponsorship from leaders inside the core business (as opposed to sponsorship only from support functions).

Governance recommendation: form a steering committee spanning corporate real estate (CRE), IT, HR and facilities management (FM) to drive workplace projects, ensuring cross functional alignment rather than siloed decision making.

George also argues organizations must move past traditional office designs that were conceived decades ago and instead adopt models aligned to how people actually work today.

The notes close with promotional links: David George's LinkedIn, the CRUX Workplace site, the IFMA Workplace Evolutionaries community, the podcast YouTube playlist, Eptura resources and past interviews, and Mike Petrusky's LinkedIn. No statistics, survey data or named client examples are included in the show notes text.

claims.claim: Successful change management rests on three pillars: employee engagement, clear communication, and sponsorship from leaders within the core business.
claims.attribution: David George, CEO & Founder, CRUX Workplace

claims.claim: Engaging employees early in the design process leads to higher acceptance and ownership of the change.
Workplace strategists must be involved from the outset to understand business processes and create effective briefs for architects and designers.
Organizations should create a steering committee including CRE, IT, HR and FM to drive workplace projects.
Many traditional office designs were conceived decades ago and no longer align with how people work today.
